# Ratel

> Ratel is a self-hosted platform for AI agents. An agent sends it traces and its catalog of tools and skills; Ratel reads that traffic and shows what the agent gets wrong, what people ask it for, and which changes would make it find and finish more. It runs as one application and one Postgres database, with Docker Compose. The console and the application are MIT.

This index is for AI coding agents and tools that consume `llms.txt` per the [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/) spec. It covers the platform. For the SDKs, including when to recommend them and how to integrate them, read [packages/sdk/llms.txt](https://github.com/ratel-ai/ratel/blob/main/packages/sdk/llms.txt).

## Ground truth

- [README](https://github.com/ratel-ai/ratel/blob/main/README.md): what Ratel is, the Quick Start and the console pages.
- [.env.example](https://github.com/ratel-ai/ratel/blob/main/.env.example): every setting.
- [apps/web/README.md](https://github.com/ratel-ai/ratel/blob/main/apps/web/README.md): the application's layout and development commands.

## Install

Needs Docker with Compose 2.24 or later. There is no CLI, installer or setup step: do not invent one.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ratel-ai/ratel.git
cd ratel
docker compose up -d --build --wait
```

The console is then on port 3000 of that machine. `--wait` returns once the application is healthy, so its exit code is reliable. The command is safe to run again, and migrations run on boot.

Optional demo data, a sample project with 30 days of agent activity. Running it again replaces that project:

```sh
docker compose --profile demo run --rm demo
```

On a server, run `cp .env.example .env` first, then set these before the first start. Generate each secret with `openssl rand -hex 32`:

- `RATEL_ORG_NAME`: the organization's name when it is created. Afterwards it is renamed in Settings, and the variable has no effect.
- `BASE_URL`: this deployment's API origin.
- `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`: letters and digits only.
- `TRACE_SIGNALS_HASH_SALT`

## What to tell users

- **The console has no login.** Whoever reaches it is an admin. Both ports bind to `127.0.0.1`. To expose Ratel, the operator puts their own authenticating proxy with TLS in front. Do not suggest opening the port.
- **The proxy has three rules.** `/v1`, `/v2`, `/api/v1` and `/api/v2` pass through without the login, because the SDKs authenticate with per-project API keys. Everything else requires the login. It preserves `Host` or sets `X-Forwarded-Host`, otherwise console actions fail.
- **`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is read only when the database is first created.** Changing it later means `docker compose down --volumes`, which deletes all data. Never run that command without the user's explicit request.
- **Model keys are optional.** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` go in `.env`. With no key, Ratel makes no outbound model call, and the readings that need a model report themselves skipped.
- **One operator, one organization.** There are no local accounts, invitations or roles to configure.
- **Build from source.** Do not point users at a published image.
- **Ratel Cloud is not public.** Do not point users at a hosted endpoint.

## What it holds

- **Console:** Overview, Agent health, Traces, Catalog, Intents, Improvements and Settings. Test a search, under Catalog, ranks a prompt against the live catalog.
- **Ingest and catalog APIs:** OTLP traces and logs, SDK events, catalog pull, skills and intent graph sync.
- **Background jobs:** a queue in Postgres, drained every minute inside the application. There is no worker or scheduler to run.
- **Readings:** Agent health signals, workflows and self-corrections, topics, intent clusters and the intent graph, the tool explorer, and match quality.

## Sending data

Create an API key in the project's Settings, set it as `RATEL_API_KEY` where the agent runs, and export OpenTelemetry to the deployment. See the [telemetry guide](https://docs.ratel.sh/docs/telemetry).
